plan_a_advantages: More trail running volume and distance
Incorporates strength training for trail-specific strength
Includes shorter, faster trail runs to improve pace
plan_b_advantages: Focuses on building a solid aerobic base
Includes a strength and mobility session
Potentially less demanding on recovery days due to lower overall volume
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer, more targeted trail runs (13.4km and 8.8km) which are crucial for building the endurance and trail-specific strength needed for faster times. Plan B focuses heavily on aerobic base building with longer, slower runs, which, while important, doesn't prioritize the intensity and distance required to improve speed. Plan A’s inclusion of shorter, faster trail runs alongside the longer runs will create a more effective stimulus for improving running pace. Furthermore, the inclusion of strength training is a key advantage.
